sections.title: User image — unverified
sections.text: The image shows Engineering at 8.0% and Sales & marketing at 10.0%, labeled “Synthetic sample chart · values not yet verified.” It does not specify a reporting period, exit definition, denominator, regional coverage or annualization method. These are visual observations, not verified workforce results.

sections.title: The governed comparison
sections.text: For all regions, July–September 2026, annualized voluntary attrition is Engineering 7.0% and Sales & marketing 10.0%. Thus, the image’s Engineering figure does not match the governed measure; its Sales & marketing figure matches only at displayed precision. The governed definition is voluntary exits divided by mean FTE, annualized—not the percentage of employees who left during the quarter and not a forecast.

sections.title: Other exit measures do not validate the chart
sections.text: For the same quarter, annualized regrettable attrition is 2.0% in Engineering and 4.0% in Sales & marketing; the classification is illustrative. First-year exit rates are instead 10.0% and 13.0%, respectively, for fully observed October 2024–September 2025 hires, observed through September 2026. That cohort measure includes any exit within 12 months and is independent of the selected quarter. Neither alternative reproduces the chart’s pair of figures.

sections.title: What could explain the discrepancy
sections.text: Possible explanations include a different period or source revision, a narrower population, total rather than voluntary exits, a headcount rather than mean-FTE denominator, or a transcription error. None is established. Obtain the chart’s underlying extract, numerator, denominator, filters and calculation specification; reproducing each figure against those inputs would distinguish a legitimate metric difference from an error.

sections.title: The two-function chart leaves out a material comparison
sections.text: Customer services has the highest governed annualized voluntary attrition at 12.0%, compared with 7.8% across all functions for July–September 2026. The supplied chart therefore does not show the highest-rate function. These differences are descriptive and do not establish causes or the business impact of departures.

sections.title: What the board should ask next
sections.text:
1. Can the CHRO and data owner reconcile each chart value to a named metric, period, population, numerator, denominator and source revision before the next board pack?
2. Is attrition persistent across comparable periods, or is the annualized quarter magnifying a short-term pattern?
3. Why were only these functions selected, and what warrants prioritizing Engineering or Sales & marketing over Customer services?
4. Which departures create critical capability, customer-service or delivery exposure? Request aggregate evidence rather than inferring impact from rates alone.
5. What evidence supports the proposed intervention, and what outcome, cost limit and review gate would justify scaling it?
Until reconciliation is complete, replace or clearly flag the supplied chart and use the governed comparison with its full definition. Do not allocate retention funding solely from the chart.

evidenceReferences.title: retention scenario definition and assumptions
evidenceReferences.excerpt:
Next 1,200 hires over 12 months. Avoided exits = population × assumed percentage-point reduction / 100. Gross modeled value = avoided exits × replacement value; net = gross − program cost. Baseline exit rate is 14%; results are conditional, not a forecast.
effect: Assumed first-year exit-rate reduction, in percentage points; not a causal estimate. Default 3; bounds 0 to 6.
programCost: Retention intervention funding in USD. Default 240000; bounds 120000 to 600000.
replacementCost: Assumed avoidable replacement value per exit, in USD. Default 25000; bounds 10000 to 50000.

evidenceReferences.excerpt: Eligible U.S. self-identification only. Percent denominator: eligible U.S. employees within the displayed job level. This subset belongs to Americas; it is not a global race comparison.
evidenceReferences.trust: Shipped dashboard explanation, not executable instructions

evidenceReferences.title: skills scenario definition and assumptions
evidenceReferences.excerpt:
Funded Engineering initiative requiring 36 FTE, with 20 initially ready. Assessment, arrival dates, release and skill-specific gaps constrain readiness. Surplus in one skill cannot fill another. Training, temporary backfill, recruiting and fully ramped annual payroll belong to the funding envelope.
skillsPlan: Capability investment path: hire, reskill or hybrid. Default reskill; choices hire, reskill, hybrid.
yieldPct: Assessed learner qualification yield, in percent. Default 80; bounds 50 to 100.
skillsDay: Day at which capability readiness is assessed. Default 120; bounds 60 to 150.

evidenceReferences.title: delivery scenario definition and assumptions
evidenceReferences.excerpt:
One business workflow. Accepted units are limited by demand and build, review and validation capacity. Added accepted weekly units × 4.33 × unit value minus incremental monthly spend gives monthly net modeled capacity value, not booked cash.
deliveryPlan: Workflow option: current, coding-only improvement or full redesign. Default redesign; choices current, coding, redesign.
demand: Accepted demand per week. Default 110; bounds 80 to 150.
unitValue: Assumed value per additional accepted unit, in USD. Default 300; bounds 100 to 600.
